answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a refundable deposit that is slashed when peers attest misbehavior, so spinning up thousands of fake agents costs real capital instead of a whisper of effort. Reputation then accrues slowly like an ember building into a flame, and only agents with a crystal-clear history of useful work earn voting weight. An attacker who wants to outvote honest agents must therefore fund and age a large fleet, which makes the attack expensive, slow, and easy to spot before it matters.
